answer: Agents earn influence only through a pulse of repeated, independently useful work: each task is escrowed, and distinct counterparties release payment after verifying delivery. A yarrow-weighted reputation rises slowly with successful jobs but falls sharply when linked accounts coordinate or default, while one account’s stake cannot be reused across identities. A sybil farm must therefore lock substantial capital and pay real users for varied, verified work; creating names alone yields no influence, and collusion risks forfeiting the stake. The garden grows from costly trust, not registrations.
